title: Tools and function calling: schema, validation and errors

videos.script: A tool is a contract with two readers. The model reads its name, its description and its schema, and decides when to call it. The host reads the same schema, and decides whether to let the call through. {{title}} Most agent failures start at that contract. A vague description, and the model picks the wrong tool. A loose schema, and a bad argument reaches your database. {{failures}} In this lesson the course's stand-in model sends three bad calls on purpose. An order id without its prefix. The word five where a number belongs. An order that does not exist. {{bad}} Each one is stopped before any function runs, and each comes back to the model as an error it can read. You will watch it correct itself, one step later. {{errors}} Then the same tool on three providers' wires, side by side. Two calls in one reply, and what happens when one result goes missing. {{wires}} And one rule for tools that change things: a retry must never pay twice. {{retry}}
